newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: EU gives S.Africa $27 million for housing project.
newsitem.headline: EU gives S.Africa $27 million for housing project.

text.p: The European Union has donated 122 million rand ($27 million) in its largest funding grant for a single project in South Africa to develop a sprawling squatter area on Durban's outskirts.

The Cato Manor area, which has the capacity to house some 160,000 people, was chosen for the single largest allocation from the total 473 million rand the EU committed this year to South Africa for development, KwaZulu-Natal officials said.

Indian residents of Cato Manor were evicted under apartheid for the land to be handed over to whites but the land was never fully utilised -- and is now mostly barren and overrun by poor informal settlements.
An agreement was reached earlier this year for land to be restored to the original owners where possible, with alternative land or compensation provided where this was not feasible.
The overall Cato Manor project, which includes building and servicing for 11,230 new homes, will cost 3.455 billion rand.

"This will involve an investment of 1.185 billion rand from the public sector, with the balance coming from the private sector," said provincial housing minister Peter Miller, adding 763 million of public sector funding had already been secured.
The EU funds will go towards building a major arterial road, five schools, libraries, sportsfields and small scale industry workshops, he said in a statement.

"...European Union funds will also be used to facilitate short-term development finance and long-term end user finance to low-income households, as well as to support various administrative and capacity building intiatives associated with the project," Miller said.
